final_proof:
Let \(C(I)\) denote the set of all continuous functions \(f:I\to\mathbb R\). For \(f,g\in C(I)\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), and \(x\in I\), define
\[
(f+g)(x)=f(x)+g(x),\qquad (\alpha\cdot f)(x)=\alpha f(x).
\]
We first check that these operations are well defined on \(C(I)\). Let \(x_0\in I\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). By continuity of \(f\) and \(g\) at \(x_0\), there are positive \(\delta_f,\delta_g\) such that, for \(x\in I\),
\[
|x-x_0|<\delta_f\implies |f(x)-f(x_0)|<\varepsilon/2
\]
and likewise
\[
|x-x_0|<\delta_g\implies |g(x)-g(x_0)|<\varepsilon/2.
\]
Hence, if \(\delta=\min(\delta_f,\delta_g)\) and \(x\in I\) satisfies \(|x-x_0|<\delta\), then
\[
|(f+g)(x)-(f+g)(x_0)|
\le |f(x)-f(x_0)|+|g(x)-g(x_0)|
<\varepsilon.
\]
Thus \(f+g\) is continuous.

If \(\alpha=0\), then \(\alpha\cdot f\) is the constant zero function and is continuous. If \(\alpha\ne0\), continuity of \(f\) at \(x_0\), applied with \(\varepsilon/|\alpha|\), gives a \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
|x-x_0|<\delta
\implies |(\alpha\cdot f)(x)-(\alpha\cdot f)(x_0)|
=|\alpha|\,|f(x)-f(x_0)|<\varepsilon.
\]
Thus \(\alpha\cdot f\) is also continuous. Since \(x_0\) was arbitrary, pointwise addition is a map \(C(I)\times C(I)\to C(I)\), and pointwise scalar multiplication is a map \(\mathbb R\times C(I)\to C(I)\).

Let \(0_I:I\to\mathbb R\) be the constant function \(0_I(x)=0\). It is continuous. Also, for \(f\in C(I)\), the function \(-f=(-1)\cdot f\) is continuous by the preceding closure argument.

We now verify the vector-space identities. Let \(f,g,h\in C(I)\), let \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R\), and let \(x\in I\). The field laws in \(\mathbb R\) give
\[
((f+g)+h)(x)=(f(x)+g(x))+h(x)
=f(x)+(g(x)+h(x))=(f+(g+h))(x),
\]
\[
(f+g)(x)=f(x)+g(x)=g(x)+f(x)=(g+f)(x),
\]
and
\[
(f+0_I)(x)=f(x)+0=f(x),\qquad
(f+(-f))(x)=f(x)-f(x)=0=(0_I)(x).
\]
Thus addition is associative and commutative, \(0_I\) is an additive identity, and \(-f\) is an additive inverse of \(f\).

The scalar identities likewise hold pointwise:
\[
(1\cdot f)(x)=1f(x)=f(x),
\]
\[
(\alpha\cdot(\beta\cdot f))(x)
=\alpha(\beta f(x))
=(\alpha\beta)f(x)
=((\alpha\beta)\cdot f)(x),
\]
\[
(\alpha\cdot(f+g))(x)
=\alpha(f(x)+g(x))
=\alpha f(x)+\alpha g(x)
=((\alpha\cdot f)+(\alpha\cdot g))(x),
\]
and
\[
((\alpha+\beta)\cdot f)(x)
=(\alpha+\beta)f(x)
=\alpha f(x)+\beta f(x)
=((\alpha\cdot f)+(\beta\cdot f))(x).
\]
Each displayed equality holds for every \(x\in I\), so equality of functions yields the corresponding identity in \(C(I)\). These are all the vector-space axioms over \(\mathbb R\). Therefore \(\bigl(C(I),+,\cdot\bigr)\) is a real vector space.
